title.zh: 我们怎样陪孩子成长：全人教育的五个理念
title.en: How We Grow Alongside Our Kids: Five Principles of Whole-Person Education

cues.zh: 谁是教育者？
cues.en: Who is an educator?

cues.zh: 老师、父母、朋友，孩子都可以是教育者。
cues.en: Teachers, parents, friends, and kids can all be educators.

cues.zh: 如果你这样想，这个视频，就是给你的。
cues.en: If you see it that way, this video is for you.

cues.zh: 学习是拥有，而不是被喂养。
cues.en: Learning is about owning, not being fed.

cues.zh: 爱因斯坦引用过一句话：“教育是在一个人完全忘记了他在学校所学的一切之后，仍然留下来的东西。”
cues.en: Einstein once quoted this: “Education is that which remains, if one has forgotten everything he learned in school.”

cues.zh: 更进一步，圣经教导我们：“凡文士受教作天国的门徒，就像一个家主从他库里拿出新旧的东西来。”
cues.en: Going further, the Bible teaches us: “Therefore every teacher of the law who has become a disciple in the kingdom of heaven is like the owner of a house who brings out of his storeroom new treasures as well as old.”

cues.zh: 我们相信，教育在于让一个人真正懂得怎样做主人，而不是被塑造。
cues.en: We believe education is about helping a person truly learn to be the owner, rather than being shaped by others.

cues.zh: 这就引出了我们关于全人教育的五个理念：权柄、目标、互教互学、引导探索、你来作主。
cues.en: This leads to our five principles of whole-person education: authority, purpose, learning from each other, guided discovery, and you are the boss.

cues.zh: 第一个理念，是权柄。
cues.en: The first principle is authority.

cues.zh: 当孩子答错了一个问题，或者不愿意参与讨论，这其实是在对权柄说“不”。
cues.en: When a child gets a question wrong, or doesn't want to join a discussion, they are really saying no to authority.

cues.zh: 我们的反应不是立即纠正、强调服从，而是带着好奇心问：你为什么这么想？你的想法是什么？
cues.en: We don't rush to correct them or insist on obedience. Instead, we ask with curiosity: Why do you think so? What's your idea?

cues.zh: 很多时候，我们发现孩子有自己的想法，并不是不懂，也不是不听话。
cues.en: More often than not, we find they have ideas of their own. It isn't that they don't understand, or that they won't listen.

cues.zh: 更重要的是，我们引导孩子思考更深一层的问题，而不只是完成一项任务。
cues.en: More importantly, we guide kids to think one layer deeper, not just to finish a task.

cues.zh: 比如：一本书为什么会被选进课堂？一个问题为什么被讨论？一件作品为什么被看见？欣赏它的标准是什么？
cues.en: For example: Why was this book chosen for class? Why is this question being discussed? Why does a work get seen, and by what standard is it appreciated?

cues.zh: 视频推荐的算法是怎样的？为什么这些视频会推送给我？AI 解决问题的方法和思路，又是从哪里来的？
cues.en: How does a video recommendation algorithm work? Why are these videos being pushed to me? And where do AI's ways of solving problems come from?

cues.zh: 这些问题，让孩子从很小就可以开始学会分辨。
cues.en: Questions like these help kids start learning to discern from a very young age.

cues.zh: 这里涉及到两个重要的教育概念：批判性素养（critical literacy）和问题化（problematizing）。
cues.en: Two important ideas in education are at work here: critical literacy and problematizing.

cues.zh: 问题化，就是把一件看起来已经有答案的事，重新变成一个问题。
cues.en: Problematizing means turning something that seems to have an answer back into a question.

cues.zh: 因为相信最终的权柄在于神，我们更愿意放下自己的权柄，释放孩子自己的想法。
cues.en: Because we believe the final authority belongs to God, we would rather set aside our own authority and set children's own ideas free.

cues.zh: 有一次，Lucas 和 Matthew 不想画命题画。
cues.en: Once, Lucas and Matthew didn't want to draw the set topic.

cues.zh: 我们问：为什么？原来，他们心里早就有了自己的画面。
cues.en: So we asked why. Each of them already had a picture of his own.

cues.zh: Matthew 画了陡峭的雪山、树林，和一个穿红衣服的小小滑雪人。
cues.en: Matthew drew steep snowy mountains, a forest, and a tiny skier in red.

cues.zh: Lucas 画了打开的天国之门：门里有爱心组成的无限符号、展开双臂的耶稣，和打开的圣经。
cues.en: Lucas drew heaven's gate thrown open, with an infinity sign made of hearts, Jesus with open arms, and an open Bible inside.

cues.zh: 足球、篮球和玩具，都被留在了门外。
cues.en: The balls and toys were left outside.

cues.zh: 一件小事，给了孩子表达自己想法的空间。
cues.en: A small thing like this gave the kids room to express their own ideas.

cues.zh: 更重要的是，让他们明白：自己被尊重，也可以学习尊重别人。
cues.en: More importantly, it showed them that they are respected, and that they can learn to respect others too.

cues.zh: 我们相信，在权柄的问题上，教育者应该是 authoritative（有权威又温暖），而不是 authoritarian（专制）。
cues.en: We believe that, when it comes to authority, educators should be authoritative, with both authority and warmth, rather than authoritarian.

cues.zh: 第二个理念，是目标。
cues.en: The second principle is purpose.

cues.zh: 我们不塑造你的孩子，我们帮助他们发现自己的价值。
cues.en: We don't shape your kids. We help them discover their own value.

cues.zh: 因为圣经教导我们：“我们原是他的工作，在基督耶稣里造成的，为要叫我们行善，就是神所预备叫我们行的。”
cues.en: Because the Bible teaches us: “For we are God's masterpiece. He has created us anew in Christ Jesus, so we can do the good things he planned for us long ago.”

cues.zh: 我们相信，孩子本身就有价值。
cues.en: We believe every child already has value in themselves.

cues.zh: 这里的“工作”，原文的意思就是“作品”；有的英文译本把它译成 masterpiece。
cues.en: The word used here means a work of art, which is why this translation says “masterpiece.”

cues.zh: 我们是神的大师之作，孩子也是。
cues.en: We are God's masterpiece, and so are our kids.

cues.zh: 在 Art Lab 里，孩子先创作：我的画，按我的想法动起来。
cues.en: In Art Lab, kids make the art first: my drawing moves the way I choose.

cues.zh: 然后，他们走进展厅，那里挂着孩子自己的作品。
cues.en: Then they walk into the gallery, where their own work hangs.

cues.zh: 这样的创作氛围和过程，会帮助孩子更多地思考：我是谁？我想表达什么？而不是去模仿别人。
cues.en: Creating this way helps kids think more about who they are and what they want to say, instead of copying others.

cues.zh: 第三个理念，是互教互学，终身学习。
cues.en: The third principle is learning from each other, and learning for life.

cues.zh: 学习者、教育者和志愿者组成一个社区，和孩子一起学习。
cues.en: Learners, educators, and volunteers form a community, learning together with kids.

cues.zh: 圣经说：“又要彼此相顾，激发爱心，勉励行善。”
cues.en: The Bible says, “And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds.”

cues.zh: 在“语言的桥”里，你教我，我教你，还有图片帮助学习。
cues.en: In Language Bridge, you teach me and I teach you, with pictures to help.

cues.zh: 更重要的是，一起讨论问题，让教育者和孩子共同学习：彼此相顾，激发爱心，勉励行善。
cues.en: More importantly, talking through questions together lets educators and kids learn side by side, considering one another and spurring one another on toward love and good deeds.

cues.zh: 第四个理念，是引导探索。
cues.en: The fourth principle is guided discovery.

cues.zh: 我们只比孩子领先一步，让探索的旅程充满乐趣。
cues.en: We stay just one step ahead of the kids, so the journey of discovery is fun.

cues.zh: 我们也领先一千步，让这段旅程安全。
cues.en: We also stay a thousand steps ahead, so the journey is safe.

cues.zh: 在圣经诗篇第 119 篇里，诗人写下了他被神引导的感受：“你的话是我脚前的灯，是我路上的光。”
cues.en: In Psalm 119, the psalmist writes of being guided by God: “Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path.”

cues.zh: 灯和光一步一步地指引我们，我们也学着这样引导孩子。
cues.en: A lamp and a light guide us one step at a time, and we learn to guide our kids the same way.

cues.zh: 在 Inception Space，我们从走廊走进梵高的房间，环顾四周。
cues.en: In Inception Space, we go from the corridor into Van Gogh's room and look around.

cues.zh: 和孩子一起探索：梵高为什么画这些人？他为什么用这样的线条？为什么常常画普通人？
cues.en: And we explore with the kids: Why did Van Gogh paint these people? Why did he use lines like these? Why did he so often paint ordinary people?

cues.zh: 第五个理念，是你来作主。
cues.en: The fifth principle is: you are the boss.

cues.zh: 孩子定方向，教育者做孩子的 agent。
cues.en: Kids set the direction. Educators act as their agents.

cues.zh: 教育者示范怎样管理 AI agent，孩子不直接和 AI agent 互动。
cues.en: Educators demonstrate how to manage AI agents. Kids do not interact with them directly.

cues.zh: 在创世记里我们看到：神赐福给亚当和夏娃，又对他们说：“……也要管理海里的鱼、空中的鸟，和地上各样行动的活物。”
cues.en: In Genesis, we see God bless Adam and Eve and say to them, “… Rule over the fish … the birds … and over every living creature …”

cues.zh: 所以在 Snake-Lab 里，你来定策略，让你的机器人和大家的同场比赛。
cues.en: So in Snake-Lab, you choose the strategy, and your bot races everyone else's in one live battle.

cues.zh: 在这里，你学会做机器人和 AI 的主人。
cues.en: Here, you learn to be the boss of robots and AI.

cues.zh: 权柄、目标、互教互学、引导探索、你来作主。
cues.en: Authority, purpose, learning from each other, guided discovery, and you are the boss.

cues.zh: 这就是全人教育的五个理念。愿我们一起，陪孩子成长。
cues.en: These are the five principles of whole-person education. May we grow alongside our kids, together.
